newsitem.title: FINLAND: Australian mining industry streching wings -analys.
newsitem.headline: Australian mining industry streching wings -analys.

text.p: Australia's mining industry, traditionally focused on domestic deposits, is increasingly looking to grow internationally, senior minerals analyst Andrew Shaw of mining company North Ltd said on Thursday.

"Australia has long been an absorber of capital... However, producers are now able to tap into a global capital base for international activities," Shaw told delegates at the Metal Bulletin Base Metal Concentrates Conference.

The development of Argentina's Alumbrera mine by North, MIM and Rio Algom signals the emergence of a small band of new major copper producers in a field otherwise dominated by North American companies, he said.
Besides acquiring 25 percent of Alumbrera, North has purchased over the past two years the Zinkgruvan zinc mine in Sweden and a majority share of Iron Ore Company of Canada.
The Zinkgruvan mine has had a 50 percent rise in its resource over the past 12 months, and the company expects it will increase further as exploration of the 240-square/km area continues, he added.
Australia produces more than five percent of the world's mined copper output, some 15 percent of its zinc and 20 percent of its lead.
